questions.question: If a vehicle is found to be over-length during a pre-trip inspection, what should the driver do?

options.text: Trim the length of the load.
Make sure flags and lights for the oversize load are fastened securely.

questions.correctAnswerText: Make sure flags and lights for the oversize load are fastened securely.
questions.explanation: If a pre-trip inspection shows an oversize load, the driver must check that all required signs, flags, lights, and reflectors are properly mounted and that all required permits are in the vehicle.

questions.question: A skid caused by acceleration can usually be fixed by:

options.text: Removing your foot from the accelerator.

questions.correctAnswerText: Removing your foot from the accelerator.
questions.explanation: Acceleration skids often happen on slippery roads. You can usually fix them by taking your foot off the accelerator.

questions.question: The best way to tell if your trailer has started to skid is to:

options.text: Use your mirrors to see if the trailer has moved out of its lane.
Release the brake pedal and push it down again.
Watch the jackknife warning light on the dashboard.

questions.correctAnswerText: Use your mirrors to see if the trailer has moved out of its lane.
questions.explanation: The easiest way to spot a trailer skid is to check your mirrors. When you brake hard, always look in your mirrors to make sure your trailer is in the correct position.

questions.question: Trailers built before 1975:

options.text: Do not need to have spring brakes.
Cannot be used on public roads.

questions.correctAnswerText: Do not need to have spring brakes.
questions.explanation: Trailers built before 1975 do not require spring brakes. When parking a trailer without spring brakes, use wheel chocks to prevent it from rolling.

questions.question: If the ABS stops working while driving, the driver should:

options.text: Use the parking brake to stop.

questions.correctAnswerText: Brake normally.
questions.explanation: If the Anti-Lock Braking System (ABS) stops working, the vehicle's basic brakes still work. Continue to drive and brake normally.

questions.question: To drive safely, it is important to know:

options.text: How far your vehicle needs to stop.
That arriving on time is the most important thing.
That other drivers will move out of your way when merging.

questions.correctAnswerText: How far your vehicle needs to stop.
questions.explanation: To drive safely, know how far your vehicle will need to stop. Stopping distance changes based on road conditions, weather, and the cargo in your vehicle.

questions.question: Drivers are usually least alert:
questions.correctAnswerText: Late at night.
questions.explanation: Drivers are usually less alert when driving at night, especially after midnight.

questions.question: When checking automatic transmission fluid, sometimes:

options.text: Your vehicle should be parked uphill.
Your vehicle should be parked downhill.
You may need to leave the engine running.

questions.correctAnswerText: You may need to leave the engine running.
questions.explanation: On some vehicles, you need to leave the engine running to check the automatic transmission fluid level.

questions.question: Using the trailer hand valve while driving:
questions.correctAnswerText: Can cause a skid.
questions.explanation: Never use the trailer hand valve while driving. Using it while the vehicle is moving can cause your trailer to skid.

questions.question: When loading liquid cargo, consider:

options.text: The air pressure in the tires.
The speed limits on the route.

questions.correctAnswerText: The weight of the liquid.
questions.explanation: When loading liquid, consider how much the liquid will expand during transit, its weight, and legal weight limits.

questions.question: What should you do if an approaching driver is using their high beam headlights?

options.text: Flash your high beam lights to tell the driver to switch to low beams.
Look toward the right side of your lane until the vehicle passes.
Pull to the side of the road until the vehicle passes.

questions.correctAnswerText: Look toward the right side of your lane until the vehicle passes.
questions.explanation: If a vehicle is coming toward you with high beams on, look away from the lights toward the right side of the road. This prevents you from being blinded.

questions.question: What color identifies service lines on trailer air connections?
questions.correctAnswerText: Blue
questions.explanation: Service lines on trailer air connections are blue. Emergency lines are red.

questions.question: What should you never do if spring brakes are activated?

options.text: Release air from the air storage tanks.

questions.correctAnswerText: Push down the brake pedal.
questions.explanation: Do not use the brake pedal if spring brakes are activated. Using both can damage the brakes.

questions.question: What must all air tanks have?
questions.correctAnswerText: A drain valve.
questions.explanation: Air brake tanks must have drain valves. These remove oil and water that build up in the tanks. They can be manual or automatic.

questions.question: What is a problem with a cargo cover that flaps while driving?

options.text: It allows air to cool the cargo.

questions.correctAnswerText: It can tear away.
questions.explanation: Cargo covers should not flap while driving. A flapping cover can tear off, exposing cargo and possibly blocking your view or others' views.

questions.question: When loading a trailer, what is important to do?

options.text: Put as little weight as possible over the axles.
Put the right amount of weight over the axles.
Do not worry about how weight is distributed.
Put weight only over the axles.

questions.correctAnswerText: Put the right amount of weight over the axles.
questions.explanation: Weight should be spread evenly in the trailer. Too much or too little weight on an axle makes control harder and can damage the axle.

questions.question: What is the maximum air leakage rate for a triple combination vehicle during a leakage test?
questions.correctAnswerText: 6 psi per minute.
questions.explanation: A triple combination vehicle must not leak more than 6 psi per minute during a leakage test.

questions.question: What is important to know about transporting radioactive materials?

options.text: Radiation passes through to other packages nearby.
Packages should be carried in the cab.
Packages should be loaded on their side.

questions.correctAnswerText: Radiation passes through to other packages nearby.
questions.explanation: Radiation spreads through nearby packages. Because of this, the number of radioactive packages that can be loaded together is limited.

questions.question: What should you do when driving?

options.text: Hide your intentions from other drivers.
Use turn signals only if vehicles are nearby.
Do not use turn signals in construction zones.
Always use turn signals to warn others of your plans.

questions.correctAnswerText: Always use turn signals to warn others of your plans.
questions.explanation: Tell other drivers what you plan to do. Use turn signals before turning or changing lanes, even if no other vehicles are nearby.

questions.question: How should you alert other drivers if you stop on the side of the road?

options.text: Turn on your four-way emergency flashers.
Keep the driver's side door open.

questions.correctAnswerText: Turn on your four-way emergency flashers.
questions.explanation: When stopped on the side of the road, turn on your four-way emergency flashers to warn other drivers.
